one_liner: Senior DOJ grants manager overseeing federal victim-services grants to Tribal communities: reviewing applications, monitoring compliance, and advising grantees.
fit_summary: This GS-13 requires one year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-12 in managing complex grants, specifically related to crime victims and survivors. Daniel's IEM consulting work may include grants or disaster-recovery funding, but nothing on file shows victim-services grant management at that level. Daniel's policy knowledge and people skills fit the liaison side of the job, not the core qualification.
eligibility: Open to the public (U.S. citizens under Delegated Examining) as well as status, veteran, and other special hiring paths, so Daniel can apply without prior federal service.
You need one year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-12: managing, monitoring, or pre-award work on complex grants or cooperative agreements related to victims or survivors of crime.
Education cannot substitute for experience, so you must qualify on experience alone.
You must complete the USA Hire online assessment within 48 hours after the 11/09/2026 closing date, or you will not be considered.
keywords: compliance with regulatory, policy, and reporting requirements
national, state, local, and tribal entities
strategy: Before applying, list exactly what you did at IEM. Apply only if you personally managed grant or cooperative-agreement work, such as FEMA Public Assistance, HMGP, or CDBG-DR compliance, monitoring, cost review, or applicant technical assistance, at a senior level for a full year.

If IEM work touched survivors, such as disaster survivor assistance or case management, describe it honestly as survivor-related program work. Don't stretch it into crime-victim experience you didn't have.

On the two-page resume, give each IEM role dates, hours per week, and title. Lead with brief grant-lifecycle bullets that use the posting's language, such as pre-award, monitoring, risk assessment, technical assistance, and compliance.
Preview the questionnaire at the posting link and answer only at levels your resume proves; the posting warns that overstating can remove you from consideration.
Block time right after 11/09/2026 for the USA Hire assessment, which covers areas such as arithmetic, data analysis, reading, and writing. The score is reused for one year.
In parallel, target GS-1109-9/11 grants roles, FEMA or VDEM grants and recovery positions, and Northern Virginia local government grants coordinator jobs, where your background is a stronger match.
resume_bullets: Grants Management Consultant [title], IEM, [MM/YYYY–MM/YYYY], [40] hrs/wk: Monitored [number] federal [FEMA PA/HMGP/other] grant projects totaling $[amount] for compliance with [2 CFR 200/program] regulatory and reporting requirements.
Provided technical assistance to [number] state, local, and [tribal, if true] applicants on eligibility, documentation, and cost review, resolving [type of] potential compliance findings.
Conducted risk assessments and reviewed subrecipient cost data across [number] sites, recommending [corrective actions/process changes] adopted by [client].
interview_questions: Describe a time you identified a compliance problem with a grantee and how you resolved it.
How would you approach a risk assessment for a multi-year, multi-site cooperative agreement?
What experience do you have working with Tribal governments or Tribal programs, and how would you build trust with them?
Walk us through how you'd review a grantee's budget modification request.
watch_outs: Experience requirement: the specialized experience is narrow (victim/survivor-related grants at GS-12 level), and you'll likely be found ineligible without true grant-management duties.
Application window: the posting opens 10/29/2026 and closes 11/09/2026, and the assessment is due 48 hours after closing.
Commute: the job is DC-based and on-site with telework, so expect a regular commute from Manassas (VRE helps).
